questions.topic: Write Then Read With An Encoding
questions.learningObjective: Explain bytes on disk vs text in memory
questions.stem: Why does a text file on disk contain bytes rather than characters?

answer.exemplar: Storage is byte-oriented, so text is encoded into bytes using an encoding; reading decodes those bytes back into characters.

questions.explanation: Storage media deal in bytes, so a str must be encoded into a byte sequence before it is written. The chosen encoding defines the mapping, and reading applies the inverse mapping to rebuild the characters. Text mode performs both conversions transparently, which is why the codec must match on the two sides.

questions.stem: What purpose does the if __name__ == '__main__' guard serve in a module?

answer.exemplar: It ensures top-level code runs only when the file is executed as a script, not when it is imported as a module.

questions.explanation: The guard separates code that should run only under direct execution from code that should be safe on import. This prevents side effects such as starting servers or opening files in importing code.
